title: Fleet Rung 44 — THE OPPOSING HANDS: the counter-grids ARM and the pegout hand proves itself. The owner ordered the opposing grids to stand on our own network — "אני רוצה לייצר עוד גרידים מתנגדים על הרשת שלנו מצד שני" (trace 1a1…c3a5) — and re-confirmed with the rung trigger (trace 1a1…c3ed). THIS FILE IS THE GATE: its presence in the repo IS the open gate (an artifact auditable in git history, never a boolean an import can flip).

questions.Q73_what_is_the_opposing_grid: A counter-grid (גריד מתנגד) is a BOTH-SIDED ladder resting on OUR side of the book, anchored to the POOL MID (our network's own price — the other side of R39's CEX anchor): when external flow pushes the market, our grid sells into strength and buys into weakness, capturing the round-trip the direction bettors pay for. The two-sided law is the essence: a one-sided grid is a direction bet, REFUSED — מתנגד means both hands.
questions.Q74_why_was_it_gated_and_why_open_now: R39/R40 booked the grids PLAN-POOL-GATED-NOT-BROADCAST — the plan was visible, the broadcast waited for the owner's word (the mesh never fires a gated rung). The owner has now given that word twice, explicitly ordering MORE counter-grids on our network. R44 arms them under law: deterministic rung ids (sha256-16, idempotent re-arm), the CAP law (per-side notional ≤ 2% of that side's depth value marked to the anchor — the impermanent-value defense), the DUST law (a rung under 1000µ keeps the grid quiet — GRID-TOO-THIN, dust never rests), and settle stays pure (the gate is an argument — byte-determinism untouched).
questions.Q75_what_is_the_pegout_hand: The second half of the real-value law ("באמת להחליף למטבע האמיתי עם ערך ולא סתם שקר"): R42/R43 queue chain-side payouts to dex/pegout-queue.json — R44 lands the KEYED CONSUMER (agents/pegout-hand.cjs, SAOS-PEGOUT-HAND/1). DEST-ALLOWLIST LAW: a chain payout fires ONLY to an estate-roster account (the 15 documented accounts of soldier_auth_audit.json); a row naming a non-estate account is REFUSED-DEST-NOT-ESTATE — never a transfer to a squatter (the live queue's 'treasury' row is exactly that refusal, booked honestly). The rail proves itself with a 0.001 STEEM self-transfer (value-neutral, receipted with txid) — the hand is real, the queue law is enforced.
questions.Q76_what_changed_in_the_kernel: dex-core.cjs v1.3.0 → v1.4.0: counterGridGate() (the artifact law), rungSizeLaw() (cap+dust sizing, both sides marked to the anchor), rungId() (deterministic idempotency), armCounterGrids() (the arm: PLAN→GATED-ARMED-BROADCAST-READY, one-sided REFUSED, thin GRID-TOO-THIN, sized rungs + broadcastPayload), GRID-ARM ops booked in the append-only ledger, the settle gate as a 6th argument, LAWS extended with the arm law + the hand law.
questions.Q77_what_stays_gated: The EXTERNAL rails stay untouched: market-exec / grid-beat / the operator CEX remain the only signing surfaces for the external chains; the mesh still never fires a keyed rail; the pegout hand fires only STEEM/SBD corridors (the estate holds the active key) and only to allowlisted dests; HIVE/HBD/BLURT payouts stay PLAN-PEGOUT-KEYED-OPERATOR (no key material — R38 law).
